The learner asks specifically: Make sure one of the senses is this meaning: school work done at home.

notes: In the plural ('i compiti'), it most commonly refers to school homework (uncountable in English), especially in the phrase 'fare i compiti' (to do one's homework).
The singular 'il compito' means an individual task or duty, or a school test ('compito in classe').

senses.definition: Schoolwork assigned by a teacher to be done at home.

examples.text: Devo fare i compiti di matematica.
examples.translation: I have to do my math homework.
examples.emotion: a bit weary but focused on the task at hand

senses.definition: Pieces of work or duties that someone is responsible for doing.

examples.text: Oggi ho molti compiti da sbrigare in ufficio.
examples.translation: Today I have many tasks to finish at the office.
examples.emotion: professional and efficient, ready to tackle a busy day

notes: While 'compiti' can mean 'tasks' in general, it is almost always used in the plural 'i compiti' to refer specifically to school homework.
It differs from 'lavoro' (job/work) because 'compiti' almost always implies an assigned duty, specifically academic for children or teenagers.
